### Phase 4 — Power Analysis & Sample Sizing

Run the power analysis to size the sample **against the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI)** — the minimum effect the study is designed to detect because anything smaller is not practically meaningful, not merely the effect a prior study happened to report. The SESOI traces to the spec's success metrics (the practical-significance threshold they imply) or to a practical-significance threshold the synthesis grounds; a prior study's reported effect in the literature matrix bounds the plausible range of the true effect and never stands in as the SESOI, because a single study's estimate is imprecise and inflated by selection on significance. The SESOI is named explicitly so the power analysis targets the effect that matters, not an inflated one that under-powers the meaningful test. An ungrounded SESOI surfaces as a `USER-CONFIRM` placeholder (the canonical `kind=effect-size`-tagged form), never invented. Ratify the significance threshold (`--alpha`, default surfaced not assumed), the target power (`--power`), the statistical test family, and the multiple-comparison correction where the design tests more than one hypothesis (R7) through the structured-inquiry channel. For each primary claim the test family is the design-keyed default or states its reason for departing from it, names a fallback test with the condition that triggers it, and names the independent unit of analysis it counts (`skills/research-suite/references/analysis-discipline.md`, Test Selection by Design); a Bayesian plan declares its model, each prior, the interval type, the practical-equivalence region and the decision threshold on its posterior mass (same file, Bayesian Plans). Compute the required sample size from the SESOI, alpha, and power; record the computation inputs and the resulting N so an independent party can re-derive it (R2). State the stopping rule explicitly — the fixed N or the sequential-analysis boundary — so optional stopping cannot inflate the false-positive rate after data collection begins. Size the study for the analysis the preregistration will run, per the rules under *Sizing for the Planned Analysis* below.

**The design MUST fix ONE budget across every compared method (R2).** The comparison allots each method the same per-trial budget, measured as equal wall-clock time AND — where an evaluation count is meaningful for the method family — equal evaluation count; when both measures apply the design MUST report BOTH so the comparison is legibly fair on each axis, and a design that reports only one axis MUST state why the other does not apply. The budget is fixed in advance and is NEVER itself tuned to favor one method, per `skills/research-suite/references/compute-utilization.md`. The comparison set the budget governs is the verified comparator ledger — the executed baselines fixed at design time and resolved to a retrievable, commit-pinned origin — per `skills/research-suite/references/comparator-provenance.md`.

**For a stochastic protocol, the design MUST preregister at least 30 independent repetitions per instance (R7).** Thirty is the floor, not the target; the count is raised until the reported summary statistics are stable when the repetition spread is wide relative to the differences under test. The preregistration fixes that the report will carry the best, mean, median, standard deviation, and worst of the primary metric per method-instance, plus convergence curves and per-instance distribution plots, per `skills/research-suite/references/empirical-comparison-rigor.md`. A deterministic method-instance runs exactly once and reports its single value, marked as deterministic.

#### Automated Configuration on Disjoint Splits

Plan parameter tuning as part of the fair comparison (R2). Where a method exposes tunable parameters, the design SHOULD tune them with an automated configurator on a designated train split under a stated tuning budget that is EQUAL across every method the comparison tunes, then evaluate on a test split that is DISJOINT from the train split — a test-split instance MUST NEVER enter tuning. The tuning protocol, the tuning budget, and the train/test split definition are recorded so the tuning is reproducible and its fairness is auditable; a comparator run at its untuned default is disclosed as a limitation. This plan is fixed here per `skills/research-suite/references/compute-utilization.md`. A study that may run an autonomous experiment campaign (`skills/research-suite/references/autonomous-experiment-loop.md`) names in the preregistration the search, admission and final untouched sets and the single untouched-set evaluation of the baseline and the final incumbent; a campaign opted into later is an R5 deviation and its result is exploratory.

#### Sizing for the Planned Analysis

The sizing records every input an independent party needs to re-derive N (R2) and covers the analysis the preregistration will run (R7), per `skills/research-suite/references/power-and-sample-size.md`:

- **Goal, sidedness, allocation.** Ratify each primary claim's inferential goal — superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence — and size for it, including the SESOI-bounded equivalence test `/research-analysis` runs on a null result. Ratify the sidedness (a one-sided test carries a written justification) and record any unequal allocation ratio in the computation.
- **Claims powered, multiplicity.** Power every primary claim at its own SESOI; the study's N is the largest requirement, and a success rule that needs every co-primary claim to succeed is sized for that joint event. Compute N at the per-test threshold the declared correction leaves, never at the uncorrected one. A secondary claim that is not sized is labelled exploratory, and an interaction claim is sized as the interaction contrast.
- **A range, not a point.** Report the required analysed N across the plausible effect range as a table or curve. When feasibility caps N, report the smallest detectable effect at that N and state that the SESOI is not powered.
- **Allowances.** Count independent units only and inflate N for within-cluster correlation; derive the collection target from the analysed N through a recorded loss rate with provenance, and fix the analysed population and the handling of missing outcomes in the preregistration. Every allowance carries provenance or stays a `USER-CONFIRM` placeholder.
- **Simulation and looks.** Where no closed form matches the planned analysis, estimate power by simulation from the stated assumed truth, check the false-positive rate under no effect first, and report the Monte Carlo error with the tool, version, and seed. A sequential rule fixes in the preregistration how many looks occur and when, with the boundary or alpha-spending function, and verifies its operating characteristics by simulation; an adaptation the preregistration does not list is a deviation (R5).
